original.title: A degree-two source multigraph preserves mortal service provenance
original.statement: Degree ≤2; each contracted mortal edge has endpoint-row ratio <4, and H1/F ratio <2.

exactAuditedStatement: The residual dated tokens admit the described recurrence-native opposite-sign multigraph of maximum degree2. Each contracted mortal edge has endpoint-row ratio<4; every H1/F edge has ratio<2. Immortal J/H2 and some other endpoints remain explicit.

Virtual E positives and their same-row p negatives are contracted as paired vertices; spliced walks retained as witnesses.

independentDerivationAndChecks: An inversion t<a, d(t)>d(a) gives the unique future-diagonal cell in rowt by coverage, bijecting H1(a, t) and F(t, a). For mortal a, p=sigma_a satisfies t<a<p<d(a)<d(t), so the same row supplies unique blocker p; since a is unborn it is B0. Equality of target row and death label recovers(t, a), giving H2 injection.

For each mortal owner, same-host p/y matching S has degree<=1 on each side by private nonreuse; same-row T joins E to p and H2 to its prebirth source p. Their row ranges exclude a and are disjoint, so T is also a matching. Different owners use different blocker labels.

The union has degree<=2 including parallel edges. Contracting an E/p T-pair splices two external endpoints of opposite sign; one external edge leaves an endpoint; no external edges delete the pair/cycle. No degree can increase above2. Same-row opposite signs cancel with zero signed row charge.

A p service at u has p<d(u)<=2u+1 and a<p<=2a+1, hence a/2<u<=2a. Remaining H2 dates equal a and D dates satisfy a<=v<=2a. Thus any splice endpoint ratio<4, independent of walk length. For H1/F, d(t)>d(a)>a and integrality/reach give2t>a, hence a/t<2. There is no zero-date endpoint with these inequalities.

The construction alone says nothing about how many isolates occur or how many edges cross a cut. In particular D vertices can become isolated after contraction; their original source does not give an automatic surviving edge.
